questions.question: C1, C2 and C3 can do a work alone in 10, 12 and 15 days respectively. All three of them began the work together but C2 left 2 days before the completion of the work. In how many days was the work completed?
questions.solution:
**Given**

C1's rate = 1/10 per day, C2's rate = 1/12 per day, C3's rate = 1/15 per day

**Formula:**

Total time = total work/combined rate of work

**Solution:**

⇒ The combined rate of C1, C2, and C3 = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/15 = 1/4 per day

⇒ Since C2 left 2 days earlier, the work done in those 2 days = 2 (1/10 + 1/15) = 1/3

⇒ Remaining work = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3

⇒ Time to complete the remaining work = 2/3 / 1/4 = 8/3 days

⇒ Total time = 2 + 8/3 = 14/3 days

**Therefore, the work was completed in (14/3) days.**

questions.question: In A mixture of 180 litres, the ratio of milk and water is 5 ∶ 1. If this ratio is to be 3 ∶ 2, then find the quantity of water to be further added.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Total mixture = 180 litres, Current ratio of milk and water = 5 : 1

**Formula:**

Quantity of water to be added = (new water quantity - current water quantity)

**Solution:**

⇒ Current quantity of water = 1/6 × 180 = 30 litres

⇒ If the new ratio is 3:2, total mixture = 180 + x (where x is the quantity of water to be added)

⇒ New quantity of milk = 3/5 × (180 + x) = 108 + 0.6x

⇒ As the quantity of milk remains the same, 108 + 0.6x = 150

⇒ x = (150 - 108)/0.6 = 70 litres

**Therefore, 70 litres of water need to be added.**

questions.solution:

⇒ Marked % above the cost = (400 - 352.94)/352.94 = 0.1333 (or 13.33%)

**Therefore, the article is marked 13.33% above the cost.**

questions.question: A man buys 13 pens for a rupee. How many pens should he sell for a rupee to earn a profit of 30 percent?
questions.solution:

Buy 13 pens for 1 rupee, sell x pens for 1 rupee, profit = 30%

Selling price = (100 + profit%)/cost price

questions.question: The average weight of 9 boxes is 61 kg. If three boxes having an average weight of 70 kg are removed, then what will be the new average weight of the remaining boxes?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Deviation of removed boxes from the initial average = 70 − 61 = 9 kg.

Total excess weight removed = 3 × 9 = 27 kg.

This excess weight is taken away from the remaining 6 boxes.

Decrease in the average of remaining boxes = 27 ÷ 6 = 4.5 kg.

New average = 61 − 4.5 = 56.5 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 56.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of 9 boxes = 61 kg

Number of boxes removed = 3

Average weight of removed boxes = 70 kg

**Formula Used:**

Sum of values = Average × Number of items

New Average = Sum of remaining values ÷ Number of remaining items

 

 Total 9 Boxes × 61 kg = 549 kg
 
 
 3 Boxes (Removed)
 3 × 70 = 210 kg

 
 6 Remaining Boxes
 6 × New Avg = 339 kg

 New Average = 339 ÷ 6 = 56.5 kg

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of all 9 boxes = 9 × 61 = 549 kg

⇒ Total weight of 3 removed boxes = 3 × 70 = 210 kg

⇒ Number of remaining boxes = 9 − 3 = 6

⇒ Total weight of remaining 6 boxes = 549 − 210 = 339 kg

⇒ New average weight = 339 ÷ 6 = 56.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 56.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

Combined average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂). This formula is highly useful for directly finding the total average when two different groups are combined.

Net Deviation Method

Net change in sum ÷ Total entities = Change in average. If a leaving group has a higher average than the original, the remaining group's average strictly decreases.

Replacement in Averages

When an item is replaced by a new one, Weight of New Item = Weight of Old Item + (Total items × Increase in average).

questions.question: Which plant tissue is responsible for the transportation of water and minerals from the soil to the stems and leaves?

__
 
• **Xylem:** 

 
 
• This is the **vascular tissue** in **plants** that conducts water and dissolved nutrients upward from the root and also helps to form the woody element in the stem. 
 
• The main function of **xylem **is to **transport water,** but it also transports some nutrients through the plant.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This is the most common type of **plant tissue **found in the **soft parts of plants.**
 
• It is responsible for the **plant's metabolic functions, such as photosynthesis, storage of starch, fats and oils, and helps in the healing and repair of wounds.**
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma:**
 
 
• This tissue gives support to the plant and is usually found in** layers beneath the epidermis**.
 
• **Collenchyma cells** are elongated cells with thickened cell walls that provide structure and **support for the plant, particularly in regions of new growth**.
 
 
 
• **Phloem:**
 
 
• This is the** living tissue** that transports the** soluble organic compounds made during photosynthesis and known as photosynthates, in particular, sugar, from leaves to the rest of the plant where needed.**
 
• This process is called **translocation**.

__
 
• **Robert Hooke:**

 
 
• **Robert Hooke** was an** English scientist in the 17th century who is often credited with first observing cells.**
 
• He used a **microscope** to observe the structure of **a thin cutting of cork **and noticed it was made up of **tiny, hollow compartments which he called "cells" because they reminded him of the cells of a monastery.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Known as the** "Father of Botany,"** Theophrastus was a Greek philosopher who studied under Plato and Aristotle.
 
• He is credited with major contributions to botany and biology, but he lived in the 4th century BC, well before the discovery of cells.
 
 
 
• **Edward Jenner:**
 
 
• Edward Jenner was an **English physician** and scientist who was the pioneer of smallpox vaccine, the world's first vaccine.
 
• While his work was instrumental in the field of immunology, he was not involved in the initial discovery of cells.
 
 
 
• **Anton van Leeuwenhoek:**
 
 
• Anton van Leeuwenhoek, a **Dutch scientist from the 17th century,** is considered the "Father of Microbiology."
 
• He greatly improved the microscope and was the first to document the existence of **bacteria, protists, sperm cells, and blood cells.**
 
• While he did significant work with microscopic observations, he did not first observe cells in cork - that was Hooke.
